observations: What I read: the full request JSON, source/original.txt, and the reading-flow page-01.json and page-01.svg as text. I opened storyboards-unnumbered/page-01.png, main-cast.png and vision-cast.png with Read and looked at them. The numbered SVGs were read as text only, not rendered, and no panel artwork exists yet.
The script matches the source page 1 word for word. The caption is in 01-1, Meera's source line is split into two balloons in 01-2, and Ananya's line is in 01-3.

In 01-2 Meera's second tail ends at about (327,1006), just outside the top-right corner of her face box (174-324 x). It points toward the mouth at (249,1130) but is capped by the 160px tail limit. It still reads as hers, but check it against the real head position at lettering.

First-reading concerns: the 'busy day' will be shown by the patients and bench in the 01-1 scene description. 'Our' and 'the rest' are supported by Ananya facing Meera's desk (off-panel left) in 01-3 straight after Meera's list of chores, so they do not need to be named.

Unnumbered scan: the caption at top-left of the wide panel is read first. In 01-2 the higher-left balloon 'Appointments...' comes before the lower-right 'I wish everything...' because of a 96px step down, and both tails go to Meera. Then the reader crosses the gutter to Ananya's single balloon in 01-3.

The plan warns that 01-2 balloon 1 to 2 runs back left-to-right. In practice the second balloon starts lower and to the right in English left-to-right order, and there is no competing balloon, so nothing is skipped.
01-3 balloon (626-881, 828-998) sits above Ananya's face (738-878, 1038-1213) with a short tail. Her planned gaze is toward the desk off-panel left, which ties her reply back to Meera.

transitions.observation: Same clinic, same morning: 01-1 shows Ananya welcoming patients at the entrance and 01-2 shows those patients queuing (backs) at the reception desk. The move inside is shown by the desk, registers and ringing phone in the scene plan.

Same reception area. Ananya is staged at the side, looking off-panel left toward Meera's desk. Her line answers Meera's 'I wish everything were easier', and her right-panel position keeps the desk to her left.

Time and place change across the page turn. The caption 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.', the office's evening window light and the laptop replace the busy morning desk, and it follows Ananya's 'Let's make the rest simpler'. Checked only on the page-02 storyboard and plan because no panel art exists yet; generating that art later stales this review.

readingReview.comparison: The first reading's natural order (caption; Meera 1 then 2; Ananya) is the same as the intended dialogue arrays and the numbered reading-flow JSON, so there is no order difference. Its open points (empty 'busy' panel, small Ananya face, Meera's tail end, 'Our' and 'the rest' not shown) are not defects. They are left to the planned artwork and checked again at artwork and lettering.

observations: What I read: the full request JSON and source. I opened storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png and both cast sheets with Read and looked at them. For the numbered order I read reading-flow/page-04.json as text.

Open point (middle row): I judge it acceptable, not a defect. In 04-2 Ravi faces screen-left and in 04-3 Ananya faces screen-right, which keeps the Ananya-left/Ravi-right axis set in 04-1 and 04-4. Ravi must speak before Ananya listens, so his close-up has to come first (left).

The cost is that the two singles face outward across the gutter, back to back. For the art: keep Ravi's gaze and turn clearly toward the left frame edge, and put the closed laptop or desk edge on Ananya's right-hand side in 04-3 so her eyeline reads as aimed past the frame at him.
All lines match the source page 4. There is no follow-up question about tiredness and no diagnosis, as the source requires.
Ravi's reaction to the reassurance is planned in 04-4 (nod, relaxed, hands on knees).
04-1: there is one balloon at top-left with its tail to Ananya on the left. Ravi on the right is silent, so the question leads straight to the middle-left balloon, which is his answer.
04-3: the narration box is a square-cornered caption, clearly not speech, above a silent Ananya. It reads as the listening pause before her reply in 04-4.
04-4: the long balloon at top-left points to Ananya on the left. Ravi on the right is silent; the planned nod is his reaction.

transitions.observation: Reception to the consultation room. The desk, window and plant in the wide 04-1 make the place change clear, and the same costumes and bag, now set down beside the chair, show it is the same visit. Checked on the page-03 storyboard and plan only.
Cut from the two-shot to Ravi's close-up from the doctor's side, facing screen-left toward her. His hand moves from his knee to rubbing his neck as he answers her question.
Reverse single of Ananya facing screen-right, hands folded, closed laptop at the desk edge. Screen direction is consistent with 04-1 even though the two panels face outward across the gutter.
Back to a two-shot with the same left/right placement. Her folded hands open into a reassuring gesture and Ravi relaxes, hands on his knees.

Place change back to reception after the consultation. The bag is back on Ravi's shoulder and the desk is familiar from page 3, but the camera reverses to Meera-left/Ravi-right. The wide desk-corner two-shot and the page break carry that reversal. Checked on the page-05 storyboard and plan only.

readingReview.comparison: The natural order matches the intended order and numbered JSON. The first reading's concerns are a missing place cue (covered by the 04-1 room art), the caption sitting between complaint and reply (an intended listening beat), the thin consultation (required by the source's no-advice rule) and Ravi's missing reaction (planned 04-4 nod). Facing the singles outward is an accepted cost of keeping the axis.

observations: What I read: the full request JSON and source. I opened storyboards-unnumbered/page-06.png and both cast sheets with Read and looked at them. The vision-cast sheet shows the specialist, partner and child as specified. For the numbered order I read reading-flow/page-06.json as text.

All captions and labels match the source page 6. Labelling both vision panels 'WELBUK VISION' is justified by the source's demand to mark future features as vision, so the repetition protects the meaning rather than being redundant.

The specialist's face box (842-947, 274-409) is only 4px right of the vision caption box's edge (x 838), with no overlap. In the art, keep his head right of the caption or re-measure before lettering.

'us' and 'our hometown' are an inclusive narrator voice taken from the source. The train art and 'may' make 'Tomorrow' read as a possible future. The partner and child are introduced only as a symbolic vision, which the source specifies.
Top row: the caption in 06-1, then the teal label stacked above the caption in 06-2. Stacking top to bottom gives an unambiguous label-then-caption order.

06-3 repeats the stack at top-left (label, then caption), with the three family face boxes to the right. 06-4 has the teal product label at top and the closing caption at the bottom-left, so they are read top then bottom.
There are no balloons on the page. The square narration boxes and the teal labels are easy to tell apart.

transitions.observation: Ravi leaves the clinic, then he is on a train by the window. The conditional caption and moving skyline show a possible later time, and the phone stays in his left hand. Checked on the page-05 storyboard and plan only.

From the real train into the vision. The pale-blue rounded vignette, the lighter palette and the 'WELBUK VISION' label mark the change in the plan, and Ravi's gaze out of the window toward the right leads into it.
Still inside the same vignette and label. The vision widens from connected clinics to Ravi's family around a wellness tablet.
Return to the present. The vignette goes away and the full palette, the familiar clinic entrance and the present-day costumes of all three come back, as the transition record says.

readingReview.comparison: The natural order matches the intended order and numbered JSON (label before caption in 06-2, 06-3 and 06-4). The first reading's concerns are an unclear narrator voice and 'Tomorrow', the partner and child not being introduced, the repeated label, specialist crowding and silent closing figures. Most are source-mandated or carried by the vignette and acting in the art. Specialist spacing is left as a check at the artwork stage.
